title: Nvidia Bids for Hugging Face, Altman Puts a Date on AGI, and Meta Settles for Billions
sources: The Rundown AI, The Neuron, The AI Field, Morning Brew, 1440 Daily Digest (Aug 26–27)
tldr: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, per The Information — tightening its grip on the AI developer ecosystem.
Sam Altman says an internal system meeting his personal AGI bar will exist by year-end; OpenAI's research chief puts the company "80% of the way" there.
Meta will pay up to $17.1–18 billion to settle child-safety lawsuits from dozens of states, with new usage limits for teens.

tips.heading: Turn a recurring ChatGPT task into a scheduled automation
steps: In ChatGPT desktop: New chat > Work > Choose project > New project, name it, and point it at a local folder.
Tell ChatGPT what the project is for and let it propose a structure (e.g. turning meeting notes into action items and weekly plans).
Feed in real input documents and have it process them once manually, then ask it to turn that routine into three scheduled automations.

tips.heading: Pressure-test a cheaper model before switching
steps: Pick one task you send to a frontier model repeatedly (e.g. summarizing calls, drafting replies).
Paste the prompt below into a fresh chat with your current model, with the task and three real input/output examples.
Run ten real inputs through the cheaper model and score them against the checklist it generates; only switch if the stated dealbreaker never shows up.
tips.prompt: I want to test whether a cheaper model can replace my current one for a repeated task. The task is [TASK]. Here are three real examples of my inputs and the outputs I accepted: [PASTE]. Ask up to three short questions first if something important is missing. Then write five pass-or-fail checks describing what a good output must contain, based only on the examples I gave you. Do not invent standards I did not show you. Give me a plain checklist I can score by hand. End with the single failure that should stop me from switching.

news.body: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, per The Information, after Hugging Face turned down a $500M Nvidia stake offer (a $7B valuation) earlier this year. Neither side has confirmed the deal; Hugging Face was valued at $4.5B in its 2023 round.
news.means: If confirmed, the "GitHub of AI" consolidates under one infrastructure vendor — worth flagging to any client who relies on Hugging Face for open models.

news.body: Sam Altman told TIME an internal OpenAI system matching his personal AGI bar will exist by year-end 2026. Research chief Mark Chen put the company "80% of the way" there; chief scientist Jakub Pachocki said the in-development "Astra" model can already do a week of research work solo.
news.means: Useful language for when a client asks "is AGI real yet" — the honest answer is internal, contested, and self-defined, not a shippable roadmap item.

beyond_ai.body: Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1–18 billion to settle child-safety lawsuits from dozens of state attorneys general over child data collection and addictive design. Sources differ on the exact structure: Morning Brew reports $12.7B guaranteed plus a conditional $5.3B (total $18B, 47 states) if TikTok and YouTube adopt matching safeguards; 1440 reports $12.1B guaranteed rising to $17.1B (52 state AGs). Meta admits no wrongdoing. New rules include a 2-hour daily cap for under-18s and no notifications during school hours.
beyond_ai.angle: A live, detailed template for what regulators now consider reasonable guardrails on youth-facing digital products — directly useful if you're advising any client with a minors-touching platform or app.
beyond_ai.starter: Have you seen the guardrails in Meta's settlement — two-hour daily caps, no notifications during school hours? That might be the new baseline regulators expect.

beyond_ai.body: Nvidia forecasts 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, well above the 45% Wall Street expected, after posting record Q2 revenue of $96.2 billion. CFO Colette Kress said actual demand is even stronger but supply is the constraint. The stock rose nearly 5% in after-hours trading.
beyond_ai.angle: A concrete demand signal if you're forecasting AI infrastructure costs or vendor lead times for clients — supply, not demand, is still the bottleneck.
beyond_ai.starter: Nvidia just guided to 70% growth next fiscal year and says demand outstrips even that — are we planning for GPU access to stay tight through 2028?

beyond_ai.body: The US Department of Justice said it disrupted a yearslong Chinese state-sponsored hacking operation that breached the DOJ, the Federal Reserve, the Senate, and NASA.
beyond_ai.angle: A sharp reminder to revisit vendor and third-party access reviews with clients in regulated or government-adjacent sectors — state-level actors are inside agencies at this scale.
beyond_ai.starter: Given the scale of the breach DOJ just disclosed, when did we last review our clients' third-party access controls?

beyond_ai.body: Flash floods killed at least 160 people in Nepal and Tibet, likely triggered by a roughly 2,000-foot glacier chunk breaking off and causing an ice avalanche into the Bhotekoshi River. Over 340 tourists are among the hundreds still missing; officials warn a second flood may be imminent.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you see the scale of the Nepal glacier floods — over 160 dead and hundreds of tourists still missing?

beyond_ai.body: The FDA approved Rasonque (daraxonrasib), the first drug from Revolution Medicines, for metastatic pancreatic cancer after chemotherapy. In trials it extended median survival to 13.2 months versus 6.7 months on chemo. Price: $39,800/month, expected to be covered by insurance.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you catch the new pancreatic cancer drug the FDA approved — it nearly doubled median survival in trials.
